intro.title: N4 Grammar — Group 1
intro.explanation: Learn N4 grammar points 1–5. These patterns are essential for the JLPT N4 level.

items.title: A とか B とか
items.explanation: Used to express multiple examples or possibilities; 'such as', 'like', 'for example'.
items.structure: Noun + とか + Noun + とか

examples.japanese: 週末は映画とか買い物とか楽しいことをしたいです。
examples.english: I want to do fun things like watching movies and shopping on the weekend.

examples.japanese: 彼女は英語とかフランス語とかいろいろな言葉を話せます。
examples.english: She can speak various languages, like English and French.

examples.japanese: この店は寿司とか刺身とか日本料理を提供しています。
examples.english: This restaurant offers Japanese dishes such as sushi and sashimi.

items.title: A は B ほど～ありません (A wa B hodo ～ arimasen)
items.explanation: Express that A is not as much as B; 'not as... as', 'not... to the extent of'.
items.structure: A は B ほど Verb/adjective ありません

examples.japanese: 今日は昨日ほど寒くありません。
examples.english: Today is not as cold as yesterday.

examples.japanese: 彼は私ほど上手に英語を話せません。
examples.english: He cannot speak English as well as I can.

examples.japanese: このレストランはあのレストランほど高くありません。
examples.english: This restaurant is not as expensive as that restaurant.

items.title: A は B ほど～ない (A wa B hodo ~ nai)
items.explanation: Expressing that A is not as ~ as B; 'not as...as'
items.structure: A は B ほど + い-Adjective stem (without い) + くない, な-Adjective + じゃない, Verb-negative potential form

examples.japanese: 山田さんは鈴木さんほど背が高くない。
examples.english: Yamada is not as tall as Suzuki.

examples.japanese: このリンゴはあのリンゴほど甘くない。
examples.english: This apple is not as sweet as that apple.

examples.japanese: 彼は私ほど勉強ができない。
examples.english: He can't study as well as I can.

items.title: A より B のほうが〜 (A yori B no hou ga 〜)
items.explanation: Comparing two things; 'B is more ~ than A'.
items.structure: A + より + B + のほうが + Adjective/Verb

examples.japanese: 田中さんより鈴木さんのほうが背が高いです。
examples.english: Suzuki is taller than Tanaka.

examples.japanese: リンゴよりバナナのほうが甘いです。
examples.english: Bananas are sweeter than apples.

examples.japanese: 冬より夏のほうが暑いです。
examples.english: Summer is hotter than winter.

items.title: い-Adjective く する/なる (i-Adjective kusuru/naru)
items.explanation: Express a change happening or making something change.
items.structure: い-Adjective (remove い) + く + する/なる

examples.japanese: 部屋を明るくします。
examples.english: I will make the room brighter.

examples.japanese: 彼の顔は赤くなりました。
examples.english: His face turned red.

examples.japanese: この料理を辛くしてください。
examples.english: Please make this dish spicy.

intro.title: N4 Grammar — Group 2
intro.explanation: Learn N4 grammar points 6–10. These patterns are essential for the JLPT N4 level.

items.title: な-adjective に する/なる
items.explanation: Used to indicate change or decision; 'to become' or 'to make' with na-adjectives.
items.structure: な-Adjective + に + する/なる

examples.japanese: 部屋をきれいにする。
examples.english: To make the room clean.

examples.japanese: 彼は元気になりました。
examples.english: He became energetic.

examples.japanese: 毎日静かにすることが大切です。
examples.english: It is important to make it quiet every day.

items.title: Noun しか～ない (Noun shika~nai)
items.explanation: Expresses 'only', 'nothing but', or 'no other'.

examples.japanese: 私はリンゴしか食べない。
examples.english: I eat only apples.

examples.japanese: 電車で行くしかないです。
examples.english: There is no other way but to go by train.

examples.japanese: 彼は一冊の本しか持っていない。
examples.english: He has only one book.

items.title: Noun に する (Noun ni suru)
items.explanation: Used to indicate a choice or decision, 'to decide on' or 'to choose'.

examples.japanese: メニューからピザにしました。
examples.english: I decided on pizza from the menu.

examples.japanese: 誕生日プレゼントに時計にするつもりです。
examples.english: I plan to choose a watch as a birthday present.

examples.japanese: 今日の午後は買い物にすることにしました。
examples.english: I decided to go shopping this afternoon.

items.title: Noun に なる (Noun ni naru)
items.explanation: To become; to change into; to turn into.

examples.japanese: 彼は医者になりました。
examples.english: He became a doctor.

examples.japanese: 子供の頃、私は先生になりたかったです。
examples.english: When I was a child, I wanted to become a teacher.

examples.japanese: 彼女は緊張して顔が赤くなりました。
examples.english: She got nervous, and her face turned red.

items.title: のために (no tame ni)
items.explanation: Used to express purpose or reason; 'for', 'for the sake of', 'in order to'.

examples.japanese: 勉強のために、図書館で静かな場所を探しています。
examples.english: In order to study, I am looking for a quiet place in the library.

examples.japanese: 彼は家族のために、一生懸命働いています。
examples.english: He works hard for the sake of his family.

examples.japanese: 健康のために、毎日運動をしています。
examples.english: I exercise every day for the sake of my health.

intro.title: N4 Grammar — Group 3
intro.explanation: Learn N4 grammar points 11–15. These patterns are essential for the JLPT N4 level.

items.title: Noun の 間に (〜no aida ni)
items.explanation: Expresses 'while' or 'during' a specific period or time.

examples.japanese: 昼休みの間に銀行に行きます。
examples.english: I will go to the bank during lunch break.

examples.japanese: 夏休みの間に海外旅行に行く予定です。
examples.english: I plan to go on an overseas trip during the summer vacation.

examples.japanese: 子供たちが学校の間に買い物に行きました。
examples.english: I went shopping while the kids were at school.

items.title: Noun ばかり (〜bakari)
items.explanation: Expresses 'only', 'nothing but', 'always', or 'just'.
items.structure: Noun + ばかり, Verb-casual + ばかり, い-Adjective + ばかり, な-Adjective + だ ばかり

examples.japanese: 彼はお金の話ばかりする。
examples.english: He talks about nothing but money.

examples.japanese: 彼女は勉強ばかりしている。
examples.english: She is always studying.

examples.japanese: デパートには高い商品ばかりだ。
examples.english: There are only expensive items in the department store.

items.title: Noun を あげる (Noun wo ageru)
items.explanation: To give something to someone; 'give', 'offer', 'present'.

examples.japanese: プレゼントをあげる。
examples.english: I give a present.

examples.japanese: 友達に花をあげた。
examples.english: I gave flowers to my friend.

examples.japanese: 父に時計をあげます。
examples.english: I will give a watch to my father.

items.title: Nounをいただく (Noun wo itadaku)
items.explanation: To receive or accept something politely; 'to receive', 'to get', 'to accept'.

examples.japanese: プレゼントをいただきありがとうございます。
examples.english: Thank you for the gift that I received.

examples.japanese: 先生からアドバイスをいただきました。
examples.english: I received advice from my teacher.

examples.japanese: このコーヒーをいただいていいですか？
examples.english: May I have this coffee?

items.title: Nounをくださる
items.explanation: Used to express someone doing something as a favor or for the benefit of the speaker.

examples.japanese: 先生が資料をくださった。
examples.english: The teacher gave me the materials.

examples.japanese: お母さんがおやつをくださる。
examples.english: My mother gives me snacks.

examples.japanese: 上司がアドバイスをくださいました。
examples.english: My boss gave me advice.

intro.title: N4 Grammar — Group 4
intro.explanation: Learn N4 grammar points 16–20. These patterns are essential for the JLPT N4 level.

items.title: Noun を くれる (Noun wo kureru)
items.explanation: Expresses that someone gives a thing to the speaker or someone close to the speaker.
items.structure: Giver + が + Receiver + に + Noun + を + くれる

examples.japanese: 友達が私にプレゼントをくれました。
examples.english: My friend gave me a present.

examples.japanese: 彼が私に花をくれた。
examples.english: He gave me flowers.

examples.japanese: 先生が私に本をくれました。
examples.english: The teacher gave me a book.

items.title: Noun を さしあげる (Noun wo sashiageru)
items.explanation: A polite way of expressing to give something.
items.structure: Noun + を + さしあげる

examples.japanese: 先生に本をさしあげます。
examples.english: I will give a book to the teacher.

examples.japanese: お母さんに花をさしあげたいです。
examples.english: I want to give flowers to my mother.

examples.japanese: お客様にお茶をさしあげましょう。
examples.english: Let's offer tea to the guest.

items.title: Noun もらう (Noun wo morau)
items.explanation: To receive or get something from someone; 'to receive', 'to get'.

examples.japanese: 友達からプレゼントをもらいました。
examples.english: I received a gift from my friend.

examples.japanese: 先生にアドバイスをもらいました。
examples.english: I got advice from my teacher.

examples.japanese: お父さんからお小遣いをもらう。
examples.english: To receive an allowance from one's father.

items.title: Noun + 中 (Noun + ちゅう)
items.explanation: Express 'in the middle of', 'during', or 'in the process of'.

examples.japanese: 彼は仕事中です。
examples.english: He is in the middle of work.

examples.japanese: 試験中、携帯電話を使ってはいけません。
examples.english: During the exam, you must not use your mobile phone.

examples.japanese: 映画を観ている最中に、彼は泣き始めました。
examples.english: In the middle of watching the movie, he started to cry.

items.title: Verb させられる (Verb-saserareru)
items.explanation: Express the passive causative form; 'to be made to', 'to be forced to'.
items.structure: Group 1 Verb: Replace ～う with ～わせられる, Group 2 Verb: Replace ～る with ～させられる, Group 3 Verb: する → させられる, くる → こさせられる

examples.japanese: 子供たちは先生に宿題をやらせられました。
examples.english: The children were made to do their homework by the teacher.

examples.japanese: 彼は会社にもっと働かせられた。
examples.english: He was forced to work more by the company.

examples.japanese: 私は友達にその機密を話させられました。
examples.english: I was made to reveal that secret by my friend.

intro.title: N4 Grammar — Group 5
intro.explanation: Learn N4 grammar points 21–25. These patterns are essential for the JLPT N4 level.

items.title: Verb させる (Verb-saseru)
items.explanation: Expresses 'to make someone do something', 'to let someone do something', or 'to cause someone to do something'.
items.structure: Group 1 Verbs: Change the last hiragana to ～せる, Group 2 Verbs: Remove ～る and add ～させる, Group 3 Verbs: する → させる, くる → こさせる

examples.japanese: 先生が生徒に宿題をさせました。
examples.english: The teacher made the students do homework.

examples.japanese: 母が私に部屋を掃除させました。
examples.english: My mother made me clean my room.

examples.japanese: 彼女にピアノを弾かせてあげました。
examples.english: I let her play the piano.

items.title: Verb た ことがある (Verb ta koto ga aru)
items.explanation: Expresses the experience of having done something in the past.

examples.japanese: 日本に行ったことがあります。
examples.english: I have been to Japan before.

examples.japanese: 寿司を食べたことがありますか？
examples.english: Have you ever eaten sushi before?

examples.japanese: 彼はマラソンを走ったことがあります。
examples.english: He has experienced running a marathon.

items.title: Verb た ときに (Verb た ときに)
items.explanation: Express an action or event that occurred at a specific time in the past; 'when', 'at the time'.

examples.japanese: 映画を見たときに、泣きました。
examples.english: When I watched the movie, I cried.

examples.japanese: 彼に初めて会ったときに、遅刻していました。
examples.english: When I first met him, he was late.

examples.japanese: 日本へ行ったときに、たくさんの写真を撮りました。
examples.english: When I went to Japan, I took a lot of photos.

items.title: Verb た ところ (Verb ta tokoro)
items.explanation: Expresses the situation right after an action has taken place.

examples.japanese: ドアを開けたところ、猫が飛び出してきた。
examples.english: When I opened the door, a cat came jumping out.

examples.japanese: 電話を切ったところ、また鳴った。
examples.english: Right after I hung up the phone, it rang again.

examples.japanese: 宿題を終わらせたところで、友達から連絡が来た。
examples.english: Just as I finished my homework, I got a message from my friend.

items.title: Verb たほうがいい (〜ta hou ga ii)
items.explanation: Used to give advice or make a suggestion to someone - 'it's better if...'.

examples.japanese: 早く寝たほうがいい。
examples.english: It's better if you go to bed early.

examples.japanese: もっと勉強したほうがいい。
examples.english: You should study more.

examples.japanese: 病気の時は、薬を飲んだほうがいい。
examples.english: It's a good idea to take medicine when you're sick.

intro.title: N4 Grammar — Group 6
intro.explanation: Learn N4 grammar points 26–30. These patterns are essential for the JLPT N4 level.

items.title: Verb ために (tame ni)
items.explanation: Used to describe the purpose or reason for an action; 'for the sake of', 'in order to', 'because of'.
items.structure:
1) Verb (dictionary form) + ために (purpose)
2) い-Adjective + ために (reason)
3) な-Adjective + な + ために (reason)
4) Noun + の + ために (reason)

examples.japanese: 試験に合格するために、毎日勉強しています。
examples.english: I study every day in order to pass the exam.

examples.japanese: 健康のために、毎日運動しなければなりません。
examples.english: For the sake of health, I must exercise daily.

examples.japanese: 仕事が忙しいために、友達と会う時間がありません。
examples.english: Because my work is busy, I don't have time to meet friends.

items.title: Verb つもり (〜tsumori)
items.explanation: Express the intention, plan, or determination to do something; 'I intend to', 'I plan to', 'I'm determined to'.

examples.japanese: 明日、友達に会うつもりです。
examples.english: I plan to meet my friend tomorrow.

examples.japanese: 今夜、晩ご飯を作るつもりです。
examples.english: I intend to cook dinner tonight.

examples.japanese: 来年、留学するつもりです。
examples.english: I plan to study abroad next year.

items.title: Verb てあげる (Verb te ageru)
items.explanation: Used to express doing something for someone; 'do something for someone'.

examples.japanese: 友達が疲れていたから、荷物を持ってあげた。
examples.english: Since my friend was tired, I carried their luggage for them.

examples.japanese: 弟は宿題がわからなかったので、手伝ってあげた。
examples.english: My younger brother couldn't understand the homework, so I helped him.

examples.japanese: 彼女が遅れそうだったから、駅まで迎えに行ってあげた。
examples.english: She was running late, so I went to pick her up at the station.

items.title: Verb て ある (Verb-te aru)
items.explanation: Indicates that an action has been done and its result is still in effect.

examples.japanese: 窓が開けてある。
examples.english: The window has been opened (and remains open).

examples.japanese: 宿題がもう終わってある。
examples.english: The homework has already been done (and remains that way).

examples.japanese: 洗濯物が全部干してある。
examples.english: The laundry has been hung up to dry (and remains that way).

items.title: Verb て いく (Verb-te iku)
items.explanation: Expresses an action that continues on into the future or a change that progresses over time.

examples.japanese: このまま練習を続けていくと、上達するでしょう。
examples.english: If you keep practicing like this, you will improve.

examples.japanese: 彼は成長していくうちに、自立心が強くなった。
examples.english: As he grew up, his independence became stronger.

examples.japanese: この会社はこれからも技術革新を行っていくでしょう。
examples.english: This company will continue to innovate in technology in the future.

intro.title: N4 Grammar — Group 7
intro.explanation: Learn N4 grammar points 31–35. These patterns are essential for the JLPT N4 level.

items.title: Verb ていただきたい (te itadakitai)
items.explanation: Express a polite request or desire that someone does something for you.
items.structure: Verb-て form + いただきたい

examples.japanese: 資料をコピーしていただきたいです。
examples.english: I would like you to make copies of the documents.

examples.japanese: この仕事を手伝っていただきたいのですが。
examples.english: I would like to ask for your assistance with this work.

examples.japanese: もしよろしければ、指導していただきたいです。
examples.english: If it is not too much trouble, I would like you to guide me.

items.title: Verb ていただく (〜te itadaku)
items.explanation: Used to express receiving someone's favor or help; 'to kindly do'.

examples.japanese: メールを送っていただいて、ありがとうございます。
examples.english: Thank you for kindly sending the email.

examples.japanese: 荷物を運んでいただいて、助かりました。
examples.english: You really helped me by carrying the luggage.

examples.japanese: 資料をチェックしていただきたいです。
examples.english: I would like you to kindly check the documents.

items.title: Verb て いただけませんか (Verb te itadakemasen ka)
items.explanation: A polite request; 'Could you please...', 'Would you mind...'
items.structure: Verb-て form + いただけませんか

examples.japanese: この手紙を投函していただけませんか。
examples.english: Could you please mail this letter for me?

examples.japanese: この荷物を持っていただけませんか。
examples.english: Could you please carry this luggage for me?

examples.japanese: 隣の部屋にいる人に静かにしていただけませんか。
examples.english: Could you please ask the person next door to be quiet?

items.title: Verb て いる (Verb-te iru)
items.explanation: Expresses an ongoing action or a state resulting from a past action.

examples.japanese: 今、本を読んでいます。
examples.english: I am reading a book now.

examples.japanese: 彼は英語を勉強しています。
examples.english: He is studying English.

examples.japanese: ケーキが冷蔵庫に入っています。
examples.english: The cake is in the refrigerator.

items.title: Verb て いる ところ (Verb te iru tokoro)
items.explanation: Describes an action that is currently happening; 'in the middle of', 'in the process of'.
items.structure: Verb-て form + いる ところ

examples.japanese: 彼は宿題をしているところです。
examples.english: He is in the middle of doing his homework.

examples.japanese: 私たちは映画を見ているところでした。
examples.english: We were in the process of watching a movie.

examples.japanese: 子供たちは公園で遊んでいるところです。
examples.english: The kids are in the middle of playing in the park.

intro.title: N4 Grammar — Group 8
intro.explanation: Learn N4 grammar points 36–40. These patterns are essential for the JLPT N4 level.

items.title: Verb ている間に (te iru aida ni)
items.explanation: Expresses 'while' or 'during the time' something is happening.
items.structure: Verb-て form + いる + 間に

examples.japanese: 映画を見ている間に、彼は寝てしまった。
examples.english: While watching the movie, he fell asleep.

examples.japanese: 子供が遊んでいる間に、私は料理を作ります。
examples.english: While the children are playing, I'll cook.

examples.japanese: 会議が行われている間に、雨が降り始めた。
examples.english: While the meeting was being held, it started raining.

items.title: Verb ておく (〜te oku)
items.explanation: Perform an action in preparation for a future situation; 'to do something in advance'.

examples.japanese: 駅で切符を買っておこう。
examples.english: Let's buy the tickets in advance at the station.

examples.japanese: 明日早く起きるために、今晩早く寝ておきます。
examples.english: I will go to bed early tonight to wake up early tomorrow.

examples.japanese: 試験前に勉強しておかないと、失敗するかもしれない。
examples.english: If I don't study in advance before the exam, I might fail.

items.title: Verb て くださいませんか (Verb-te kudasaimasen ka)
items.explanation: Polite request for asking someone for a favor.
items.structure: Verb in て-form + くださいませんか

examples.japanese: コーヒーを飲んでくださいませんか。
examples.english: Would you please drink some coffee?

examples.japanese: ドアを閉めてくださいませんか。
examples.english: Would you please close the door?

examples.japanese: 明日お昼に会ってくださいませんか。
examples.english: Would you please meet me at lunch tomorrow?

items.title: Verb て くださる (Verb-te kudasaru)
items.explanation: Expresses gratitude for receiving someone's favor; 'to kindly do'.

examples.japanese: 先生が手伝ってくださる。
examples.english: The teacher kindly helps.

examples.japanese: お母さんが美味しい料理を作ってくださる。
examples.english: My mother kindly cooks delicious meals.

examples.japanese: 友達が私を駅まで送ってくださる。
examples.english: My friend kindly gives me a ride to the station.

items.title: Verb て くる (Verb te kuru)
items.explanation: An action that starts in the past and continues to the present or future; 'come to', 'begin to', 'become'.

examples.japanese: 最近、日本語が分かってくるようになりました。
examples.english: Recently, I've come to understand Japanese.

examples.japanese: 寒くなってきたので、コートを着ましょう。
examples.english: Since it's gotten cold, let's put on a coat.

examples.japanese: 雨がやんできました。
examples.english: The rain has stopped (and it's cleared up).

intro.title: N4 Grammar — Group 9
intro.explanation: Learn N4 grammar points 41–45. These patterns are essential for the JLPT N4 level.

items.title: Verb てくれませんか (〜te kuremasen ka)
items.explanation: A polite way to request someone to do something for you; 'Could you please', 'Would you please', 'Won't you'.
items.structure: Verb-て form + くれませんか

examples.japanese: ドアを開けてくれませんか。
examples.english: Could you please open the door?

examples.japanese: これを見てくれませんか。
examples.english: Would you please take a look at this?

examples.japanese: 手伝ってくれませんか。
examples.english: Won't you help me?

items.title: Verb て くれる (Verb-te kureru)
items.explanation: Expresses that someone does something for the speaker (or another person in speaker's group); 'to do something for me/us'.

examples.japanese: 友達が宿題を手伝ってくれました。
examples.english: My friend helped me with my homework.

examples.japanese: 弟が部屋を掃除してくれた。
examples.english: My younger brother cleaned the room for me.

examples.japanese: 先生が質問に答えてくれます。
examples.english: The teacher answers my questions for me.

items.title: Verb て + さしあげる (Verb TE sashiageru)
items.explanation: A polite way to express giving or doing something for someone.

examples.japanese: お茶を入れてさしあげます。
examples.english: I will prepare and serve tea (for you).

examples.japanese: メッセージを送ってさしあげました。
examples.english: I have sent the message (for you).

examples.japanese: 荷物を持ってさしあげましょうか。
examples.english: Shall I carry the luggage (for you)?

items.title: Verb てしまう (〜te shimau)
items.explanation: Expresses unintentional actions or actions with regrettable outcomes; 'to end up doing', 'to accidentally do'.

examples.japanese: ケーキを全部食べてしまった。
examples.english: I ended up eating the whole cake.

examples.japanese: 宿題を忘れてしまいました。
examples.english: I accidentally forgot my homework.

examples.japanese: 彼に秘密を言ってしまった。
examples.english: I accidentally told him the secret.

items.title: Verb て ほしい (Verb-te hoshii)
items.explanation: Express a desire for someone else to do something; 'I want (someone) to'.

examples.japanese: 子供にもっと勉強してほしい。
examples.english: I want my child to study more.

examples.japanese: 彼にもっと早く来てほしい。
examples.english: I want him to come earlier.

examples.japanese: 友達にその本を読んでほしい。
examples.english: I want my friend to read that book.

intro.title: N4 Grammar — Group 10
intro.explanation: Learn N4 grammar points 46–50. These patterns are essential for the JLPT N4 level.

items.title: Verb てみる (〜te miru)
items.explanation: Used to express 'try to' or 'attempt to do'.

examples.japanese: この料理を作ってみます。
examples.english: I will try to make this dish.

examples.japanese: その服を着てみてください。
examples.english: Please try on those clothes.

examples.japanese: 新しいレストランに行ってみよう。
examples.english: Let's try going to the new restaurant.

items.title: Verb てもらいたい (～te moraitai)
items.explanation: Express a desire to receive a favor or service from someone else.

examples.japanese: この荷物を運んでもらいたいです。
examples.english: I want you to carry this luggage for me.

examples.japanese: 彼にそのニュースを教えてもらいたい。
examples.english: I want him to tell me the news.

examples.japanese: 友達に日本語を教えてもらいたい。
examples.english: I want my friend to teach me Japanese.

items.title: Verb て もらう (Verb-te morau)
items.explanation: Express receiving a favor or action from someone.

examples.japanese: 友達に宿題を手伝ってもらった。
examples.english: I had my friend help me with my homework.

examples.japanese: 母に部屋を掃除してもらいました。
examples.english: I had my mother clean my room.

examples.japanese: 彼に荷物を持ってもらいたい。
examples.english: I want him to carry my luggage for me.

items.title: Verb てもらえませんか (～te moraemasen ka)
items.explanation: A polite way to ask for a favor or request someone to do something.
items.structure: Verb-て form + もらえませんか

examples.japanese: この手紙を見てもらえませんか。
examples.english: Could you take a look at this letter for me?

examples.japanese: 荷物を持ってもらえませんか。
examples.english: Could you carry this luggage for me?

examples.japanese: 部屋を掃除してもらえませんか。
examples.english: Could you clean the room for me?

items.title: Verb ない ことがある (Verb-nai koto ga aru)
items.explanation: Expresses that something doesn't always happen or there are occasions when it doesn't happen.

examples.japanese: 彼は会議に出席しないことがある。
examples.english: There are times when he doesn't attend meetings.

examples.japanese: この電車は定刻に来ないことがある。
examples.english: There are occasions when this train doesn't come on time.

examples.japanese: 私は朝食を食べないことがある。
examples.english: There are times when I don't eat breakfast.

intro.title: N4 Grammar — Group 11
intro.explanation: Learn N4 grammar points 51–55. These patterns are essential for the JLPT N4 level.

items.title: Verb ない + ことにする (Verb nai koto ni suru)
items.explanation: To decide not to do something.
items.structure: Verb-ない form + ことにする

examples.japanese: 明日のパーティーに行かないことにする。
examples.english: I've decided not to go to tomorrow's party.

examples.japanese: そのケーキを食べないことにします。
examples.english: I've decided not to eat that cake.

examples.japanese: 今日はジョギングをしないことにする。
examples.english: I've decided not to go jogging today.

items.title: Verb ない ことになる (Verb nai koto ni naru)
items.explanation: Expresses a result; 'end up not', 'it will become that', 'it would mean that'.

examples.japanese: 今日彼が来ないことになると、私たちの予定はキャンセルされます。
examples.english: If he doesn't come today, our plans will be canceled.

examples.japanese: このプロジェクトが進まないことになると、収益が減るでしょう。
examples.english: If this project doesn't progress, it would mean that revenue will decrease.

examples.japanese: 彼女は試験に合格しないことになると、卒業が遅れます。
examples.english: If she ends up not passing the exam, her graduation will be delayed.

items.title: Verb ないほうがいい (Verb nai hou ga ii)
items.explanation: Expresses the idea that it is better not to do something.

examples.japanese: この薬は飲まないほうがいいです。
examples.english: It's better not to take this medicine.

examples.japanese: 急いでいるときは、走らないほうがいい。
examples.english: When you're in a hurry, it's better not to run.

examples.japanese: 彼に秘密を知られたくなければ、話さないほうがいい。
examples.english: If you don't want him to know your secret, it's better not to tell him.

items.title: Verb ながら (〜nagara)
items.explanation: Expresses 'while' or 'as' in the sense of doing two things simultaneously.

examples.japanese: テレビを見ながら宿題をしました。
examples.english: I did my homework while watching television.

examples.japanese: 音楽を聞きながら料理をしました。
examples.english: I cooked while listening to music.

examples.japanese: 歩きながらスマホを見るのは危険です。
examples.english: Looking at your smartphone while walking is dangerous.

items.title: Verb なさい (〜nasai)
items.explanation: A command form used to give orders or instructions; 'Please do', 'Do this'.

examples.japanese: 部屋を掃除しなさい。
examples.english: Clean your room.

examples.japanese: 勉強しなさい。
examples.english: Study.

examples.japanese: 早く起きなさい。
examples.english: Wake up early.

intro.title: N4 Grammar — Group 12
intro.explanation: Learn N4 grammar points 56–60. These patterns are essential for the JLPT N4 level.

items.title: Verb にくい (〜nikui)
items.explanation: Express difficulty or complexity; 'hard to', 'difficult to', 'not easily'.

examples.japanese: この字は読みにくいです。
examples.english: This character is hard to read.

examples.japanese: このドアは開けにくい。
examples.english: This door is difficult to open.

examples.japanese: 彼の字は読みにくい。
examples.english: His handwriting is hard to read.

items.title: Verb やすい (〜yasui)
items.explanation: Indicates that something is easy to do; 'easy to', 'easy for'.

examples.japanese: この本は読みやすいです。
examples.english: This book is easy to read.

examples.japanese: このシャツは着やすい。
examples.english: This shirt is easy to wear.

examples.japanese: 彼は話しやすい人です。
examples.english: He is an easy person to talk to.

items.title: Verb ようと思う (Verb-you to omou)
items.explanation: Express intention or plan to do something; 'I think I will', 'I plan to', 'I intend to'.

examples.japanese: 明日、映画を見ようと思います。
examples.english: I think I will watch a movie tomorrow.

examples.japanese: 週末に友達と遊ぼうと思っています。
examples.english: I plan to hang out with friends on the weekend.

examples.japanese: 勉強をもっと頑張ろうと思う。
examples.english: I intend to study harder.

items.title: Verb ように (〜you ni)
items.explanation: Used to express 'like', 'as if', 'in order to', or 'so that'.
items.structure: Examples: Noun + のように / Verb-casual + ように / い-adjective + ように

examples.japanese: 彼女は鳥のように軽やかに踊る。
examples.english: She dances lightly like a bird.

examples.japanese: 覚えたことを忘れないように、毎日復習しましょう。
examples.english: In order not to forget what you've learned, let's review every day.

examples.japanese: 歌手になるように、毎日歌の練習をしています。
examples.english: In order to become a singer, I practice singing every day.

items.title: Verb ようにする (Verb ~you ni suru)
items.explanation: Make an effort to; try to; see to it that; ensure that.

examples.japanese: 毎日運動するようにしています。
examples.english: I try to exercise every day.

examples.japanese: 早く寝るようにしてください。
examples.english: Please try to go to bed early.

examples.japanese: 約束を守るようにします。
examples.english: I will make sure to keep my promise.

intro.title: N4 Grammar — Group 13
intro.explanation: Learn N4 grammar points 61–65. These patterns are essential for the JLPT N4 level.

items.title: Verb ようになる (〜you ni naru)
items.explanation: Express a change in ability, situation or state; 'become able to', 'come to', 'begin to'.

examples.japanese: 日本語が話せるようになりました。
examples.english: I have become able to speak Japanese.

examples.japanese: 最近、早く寝るようになった。
examples.english: Recently, I have come to go to bed early.

examples.japanese: 彼はピアノを弾けるようになりました。
examples.english: He has become able to play the piano.

items.title: Verb ように言う (Verb-you ni iu)
items.explanation: Tell someone to do something; 'tell to do', 'instruct to do'.

examples.japanese: 先生は私たちに宿題をやるように言いました。
examples.english: The teacher told us to do our homework.

examples.japanese: 母は弟に部屋を片付けるように言いました。
examples.english: My mother told my younger brother to clean his room.

examples.japanese: 上司は私に報告書を提出するように言いました。
examples.english: My boss told me to submit the report.

items.title: Verb られる (〜rareru)
items.explanation: Expresses passive voice or potential form for verbs.
items.structure: う-verb (passive): Replace the final う with われる / る-verb (passive & potential): Replace る with られる / Irregular: する → される, くる → こられる

examples.japanese: 彼は先生に褒められました。
examples.english: He was praised by the teacher.

examples.japanese: 彼は友達に笑われました。
examples.english: He was laughed at by his friends.

examples.japanese: 映画は観られましたか？
examples.english: Were you able to watch the movie?

items.title: Verb る ことがある (〜ru koto ga aru)
items.explanation: Used to express that something happens sometimes or has happened before.

examples.japanese: 彼は遅刻することがあります。
examples.english: He is sometimes late.

examples.japanese: 私は寝坊することがあります。
examples.english: I sometimes oversleep.

examples.japanese: 彼女は歌を歌うことがあります。
examples.english: She sometimes sings songs.

items.title: Verb ることができる (〜ru koto ga dekiru)
items.explanation: Express ability or possibility of doing an action; 'can', 'be able to', 'is possible'.

examples.japanese: 私は日本語を話すことができます。
examples.english: I can speak Japanese.

examples.japanese: 彼はギターを弾くことができます。
examples.english: He can play the guitar.

examples.japanese: この問題を解決することができますか？
examples.english: Can you solve this problem?

intro.title: N4 Grammar — Group 14
intro.explanation: Learn N4 grammar points 66–70. These patterns are essential for the JLPT N4 level.

items.title: Verb ることにする (〜ru koto ni suru)
items.explanation: Decide to do something, make a decision.

examples.japanese: 来週、ジムに行くことにしました。
examples.english: I decided to go to the gym next week.

examples.japanese: この靴を買うことにしました。
examples.english: I decided to buy these shoes.

examples.japanese: 毎日、散歩をすることにしました。
examples.english: I decided to take a walk every day.

items.title: Verb る ことになる (〜ru koto ni naru)
items.explanation: Indicates that something has been decided or arranged; 'it has been decided that', 'it turns out that'.

examples.japanese: 今日は会議がなくなることになりました。
examples.english: It has been decided that there will be no meeting today.

examples.japanese: 来週、友達と旅行することになった。
examples.english: It has been arranged that I will travel with my friends next week.

examples.japanese: 彼女が今度のプロジェクトのリーダーになることになりました。
examples.english: It has been decided that she will be the leader of the next project.

items.title: Verb るときに (〜ru toki ni)
items.explanation: Describes the time when a certain action takes place; 'when', 'at the time'.

examples.japanese: 映画を見るときに、ポップコーンを食べます。
examples.english: When I watch a movie, I eat popcorn.

examples.japanese: 寝るときに、部屋の電気を消します。
examples.english: When I go to bed, I turn off the room lights.

examples.japanese: 運動するときに、水分補給が大切です。
examples.english: When exercising, it's important to stay hydrated.

items.title: Verb る ところ (Verb-ru tokoro)
items.explanation: Expresses the state or moment when an action is about to happen or is happening.

examples.japanese: 彼は食べるところです。
examples.english: He is in the process of eating.

examples.japanese: 私は出かけるところです。
examples.english: I am just about to leave.

examples.japanese: 彼女は泣くところでした。
examples.english: She was on the verge of crying.

items.title: Verb 出す (~dasu)
items.explanation: Express the action of taking something out, starting an action, or emphasizing a verb.

examples.japanese: 本を棚から出してください。
examples.english: Please take the book out from the shelf.

examples.japanese: 彼は部屋から急いで出ました。
examples.english: He rushed out of the room.

examples.japanese: 授業が始まる前に宿題を出してください。
examples.english: Submit your homework before class starts.

intro.title: N4 Grammar — Group 15
intro.explanation: Learn N4 grammar points 71–75. These patterns are essential for the JLPT N4 level.

items.title: Verb 方 (〜hou)
items.explanation: Indicates the way or method of doing something; often read as '～かた' ('how to', 'the way of').

examples.japanese: 誰かがケーキの作り方を知っていますか？
examples.english: Does anyone know how to make a cake?

examples.japanese: 彼女は英語の話し方を学んでいます。
examples.english: She is learning how to speak English.

examples.japanese: このパソコンの使い方を教えてください。
examples.english: Please teach me how to use this computer.

items.title: Verb 終わる (〜owaru)
items.explanation: Verbal action is completed; 'to finish', 'to end'.

examples.japanese: 映画が終わったら、家に帰ります。
examples.english: When the movie finishes, I'll go home.

examples.japanese: 仕事が終わるまで、待ってください。
examples.english: Please wait until the work is finished.

examples.japanese: パーティーはもうすぐ終わります。
examples.english: The party will be over soon.

items.title: Verb + 続ける (つづける, tsuzukeru)
items.explanation: To continue doing or to keep doing an action.

examples.japanese: 彼は毎日ジムで運動を続けています。
examples.english: He continues to exercise at the gym every day.

examples.japanese: 彼女は勉強を続けるために図書館に行きました。
examples.english: She went to the library to continue studying.

examples.japanese: 私たちは雨にも関わらず散歩を続けました。
examples.english: We continued walking despite the rain.

items.title: ～かしら (〜kashira)
items.explanation: Indicates uncertainty or doubt; 'I wonder', 'I'm not sure'.
items.structure: Verb-casual + かしら, い-Adjective + かしら, な-Adjective + かしら, Noun + かしら

examples.japanese: 今日は雨が降るかしら？
examples.english: I wonder if it will rain today?

examples.japanese: このケーキは美味しいかしら？
examples.english: I wonder if this cake is delicious?

examples.japanese: 彼は病気かしら？
examples.english: I wonder if he is sick?

items.title: ～かどうか (〜ka dou ka)
items.explanation: Used to express 'whether' or 'if' in indirect questions or statements.
items.structure: Verb-casual + かどうか, い-Adjective + かどうか, な-Adjective + (だ)かどうか, Noun + (だ)かどうか

examples.japanese: 彼が来るかどうか知りません。
examples.english: I don't know if he will come or not.

examples.japanese: この本が面白いかどうか教えてください。
examples.english: Please tell me if this book is interesting or not.

examples.japanese: 彼女が綺麗だかどうかは分かりません。
examples.english: I don't know whether she is beautiful or not.

intro.title: N4 Grammar — Group 16
intro.explanation: Learn N4 grammar points 76–80. These patterns are essential for the JLPT N4 level.

items.title: ～かなあ (〜kanaa)
items.explanation: Expresses uncertainty or wonder; 'I wonder', 'I'm not sure'.
items.structure: Verb-casual + かなあ, い-Adjective + かなあ, (な-Adjective/Noun) + (だ) + かなあ

examples.japanese: 明日雨が降るかなあ。
examples.english: I wonder if it will rain tomorrow.

examples.japanese: このケーキは美味しいかなあ。
examples.english: I wonder if this cake is delicious.

examples.japanese: 彼は病気かなあ。
examples.english: I wonder if he is sick.

items.title: ～かもしれない (〜kamoshirenai)
items.explanation: Express uncertainty; 'maybe', 'might', 'possibly'.
items.structure: Verb-casual + かもしれない, い-Adjective + かもしれない, な-Adjective + だかもしれない, Noun + だかもしれない

examples.japanese: 明日雨が降るかもしれない。
examples.english: It might rain tomorrow.

examples.japanese: このケーキは美味しいかもしれない。
examples.english: This cake might be delicious.

examples.japanese: 彼が病気かもしれない。
examples.english: He might be sick.

items.title: ～から (〜kara)
items.explanation: Express a reason or cause; 'because', 'since', 'due to'.
items.structure: Verb-casual + から, い-Adjective + から, な-Adjective + だから, Noun + だから

examples.japanese: 雨が降るから、傘を持って行ってください。
examples.english: Because it's raining, please bring an umbrella.

examples.japanese: このケーキは美味しいから、みんな食べるでしょう。
examples.english: Because this cake is delicious, everyone will probably eat it.

examples.japanese: 彼は病気だから、学校を休みます。
examples.english: He will be absent from school because he is sick.

items.title: ～けれど (〜keredo)
items.explanation: Indicate a soft contrast or contradiction; 'but', 'however'.
items.structure: Verb-casual + けれど, い-Adjective + けれど, な-Adjective + だけれど, Noun + だけれど

examples.japanese: 今日は忙しいけれど、明日はもっと時間がある。
examples.english: I'm busy today, but I have more time tomorrow.

examples.japanese: このレストランは高いけれど、料理が美味しい。
examples.english: This restaurant is expensive, but the food is delicious.

examples.japanese: 彼は若いけれど、とても経験豊富だ。
examples.english: He is young, but he is very experienced.

items.title: ～させてください (〜sasete kudasai)
items.explanation: Express a polite request to allow or permit someone to do something.

examples.japanese: もう少し考えさせてください。
examples.english: Please let me think a little more.

examples.japanese: 写真を撮らせてください。
examples.english: Please let me take a photo.

examples.japanese: もうちょっと練習させてください。
examples.english: Please let me practice a little more.

intro.title: N4 Grammar — Group 17
intro.explanation: Learn N4 grammar points 81–85. These patterns are essential for the JLPT N4 level.

items.title: ～し、～し、～ (〜shi, 〜shi, 〜)
items.explanation: Express multiple reasons or characteristics; 'and', 'because', 'since'.
items.structure: Verb-casual + し, い-Adjective + し, な-Adjective + だし, Noun + だし

examples.japanese: 彼は若いし、元気だし、フレンドリーだし、みんなと仲良くなれると思います。
examples.english: He is young, energetic, friendly, and I think he can get along with everyone.

examples.japanese: このレストランは料理が美味しいし、雰囲気がいいし、価格も手頃だからお勧めです。
examples.english: I recommend this restaurant because the food is delicious, the atmosphere is nice, and the prices are reasonable.

examples.japanese: 彼女は勉強ができるし、スポーツも得意だし、性格もいい。
examples.english: She is good at studying, good at sports, and has a good personality.

items.title: ～すぎる (〜sugiru)
items.explanation: Expresses that something is excessive or overdone; 'too much', 'too', 'over'.
items.structure: Verb-stem + すぎる, い-Adjective (remove い) + すぎる, な-Adjective + すぎる

examples.japanese: この部屋は暑すぎる。
examples.english: This room is too hot.

examples.japanese: 彼は早く来すぎた。
examples.english: He came too early.

examples.japanese: この箱は重すぎて持ち上げられない。
examples.english: This box is too heavy to lift.

items.title: ～ずつ (〜zutsu)
items.explanation: Indicates equal distribution; 'each', 'per', 'apiece'.

examples.japanese: りんごを2つずつ配ります。
examples.english: I will distribute 2 apples each.

examples.japanese: 私たちは週に一度ずつ掃除をします。
examples.english: We each clean once per week.

examples.japanese: みんなは同じ距離を一歩ずつ歩いた。
examples.english: Everyone walked the same distance, one step at a time.

items.title: ～そうだ (〜sou da)
items.explanation: Express the appearance, seeming, or feeling of something; 'looks like', 'seems', 'appears'.
items.structure: Verb-ますstem + そうだ, い-Adjective (without い) + そうだ, な-Adjective + そうだ

examples.japanese: その花はとてもきれいそうだ。
examples.english: That flower looks very beautiful.

examples.japanese: 彼は疲れそうだ。
examples.english: He looks tired.

examples.japanese: この本は面白そうだ。
examples.english: This book looks interesting.

items.title: そんな (sonna) + Noun
items.explanation: Expresses 'that kind/type of'; referring to something near the listener or previously mentioned.

examples.japanese: そんな話、信じられない。
examples.english: I can't believe that kind of story.

examples.japanese: そんな映画、見たくない。
examples.english: I don't want to watch that kind of movie.

intro.title: N4 Grammar — Group 18
intro.explanation: Learn N4 grammar points 86–90. These patterns are essential for the JLPT N4 level.

items.title: そんなに～ (sonna ni〜)
items.explanation: Expresses 'not so much', 'not that', or 'not so ~'.
items.structure: そんなに + Verb-negation, そんなに + Adjective-negation

examples.japanese: そんなに急がなくてもいいですよ。
examples.english: You don't have to hurry that much.

examples.japanese: そんなに難しくない問題だと思います。
examples.english: I don't think the problem is that difficult.

examples.japanese: 彼女はそんなに背が高くありません。
examples.english: She is not that tall.

items.title: ～たらいい (〜tara ii)
items.explanation: Expressing a desire or suggestion for a particular outcome; 'it would be good if', 'should', 'I hope'.

examples.japanese: もっと勉強したらいいですよ。
examples.english: It would be good if you studied more.

examples.japanese: 雨が止んだらいいな。
examples.english: I hope the rain stops.

examples.japanese: 早く元気になったらいいですね。
examples.english: It would be good if you got well soon.

items.title: ～たら いかがですか (〜tara ikaga desu ka)
items.explanation: Making polite suggestions; 'how about if', 'what if', 'it would be good if'.
items.structure: Verb-casual, past + たら いかがですか, い-Adjective + かったら いかがですか, な-Adjective + だったら いかがですか, Noun + だったら いかがですか

examples.japanese: 図書館に行ったらいかがですか。
examples.english: How about going to the library?

examples.japanese: 寒かったらカーディガンを着るのはいかがですか。
examples.english: How about wearing a cardigan if it's cold?

examples.japanese: 部屋が暗かったら照明を付けるのはいかがですか。
examples.english: What if you turn on the light if the room is dark?

items.title: ～たら どうですか (〜tara doudesuka)
items.explanation: Express a suggestion or advice; 'what if', 'how about', 'why don't you'.
items.structure: Verb-た form + ら どうですか

examples.japanese: スキーに行ったらどうですか？
examples.english: How about going skiing?

examples.japanese: 少し休んだらどうですか？
examples.english: What if you take a little break?

examples.japanese: この本を読んだらどうですか？
examples.english: Why don't you read this book?

items.title: ～たり～たり (〜tari 〜tari)
items.explanation: Used to list multiple actions or states; 'doing things like', 'and so on', 'etc.'
items.structure: Verb-ta + り + next verb-ta + り, い-Adjective + かったり + next verb-ta + り, な-Adjective + だったり + next verb-ta + り, Noun + だったり + next verb-ta + り

examples.japanese: 週末は映画を観たり、本を読んだりする。
examples.english: On weekends, I do things like watching movies and reading books.

examples.japanese: 彼女は料理が上手だったり、歌がうまかったりする。
examples.english: She is good at things like cooking and singing.

examples.japanese: このリゾートではスキーをしたり、温泉に入ったりできる。
examples.english: At this resort, you can do things like skiing and going to hot springs.

intro.title: N4 Grammar — Group 19
intro.explanation: Learn N4 grammar points 91–95. These patterns are essential for the JLPT N4 level.

items.title: ～だろう (〜darou)
items.explanation: Express probability, likelihood or certainty; 'probably', 'maybe', 'I think'.
items.structure: Verb-casual + だろう, い-Adjective (drop い) + だろう, な-Adjective + だろう, Noun + だろう

examples.japanese: 明日は晴れるだろう。
examples.english: It will probably be sunny tomorrow.

examples.japanese: 彼は忙しいだろう。
examples.english: He is probably busy.

examples.japanese: この本は面白いだろう。
examples.english: This book is probably interesting.

items.title: ～っていう (〜tte iu)
items.explanation: Used to quote, define, or specify a noun.

examples.japanese: ピザっていう料理が大好きです。
examples.english: I love the dish called pizza.

examples.japanese: 彼っていう男性はすごく面白いです。
examples.english: That man (called ‘kare’) is really interesting.

examples.japanese: この映画っていうのは本当に感動的だよ。
examples.english: This movie, I mean, is really touching.

items.title: ～で (〜de)
items.explanation: Indicates the means, method, or place.

examples.japanese: 私は自転車で学校に行きます。
examples.english: I go to school by bicycle.

examples.japanese: 彼は日本語で手紙を書いた。
examples.english: He wrote a letter in Japanese.

examples.japanese: 鉛筆で絵を描きました。
examples.english: I drew a picture with a pencil.

items.title: ～でしょう (〜deshou)
items.explanation: A conjecture or probability; 'probably', 'I think', 'it seems'.
items.structure: Verb-ますstem + でしょう, い-Adjective + でしょう, な-Adjective + でしょう, Noun + でしょう

examples.japanese: 明日は晴れでしょう。
examples.english: It will probably be sunny tomorrow.

examples.japanese: 彼は元気でしょう。
examples.english: He is probably fine.

examples.japanese: この本は面白いでしょう。
examples.english: This book is probably interesting.

items.title: ～てはいけない (〜te wa ikenai)
items.explanation: Expresses prohibition; 'must not', 'cannot'.

examples.japanese: 公園でたばこを吸ってはいけない。
examples.english: You must not smoke in the park.

examples.japanese: ここで写真を撮ってはいけない。
examples.english: You cannot take pictures here.

examples.japanese: 図書館で大きな声を出してはいけない。
examples.english: You must not speak loudly in the library.

intro.title: N4 Grammar — Group 20
intro.explanation: Learn N4 grammar points 96–100. These patterns are essential for the JLPT N4 level.

items.title: ～てもいい (〜temo ii)
items.explanation: To give or ask permission; 'it's okay to', 'may', 'can'.

examples.japanese: ここで写真を撮ってもいいですか。
examples.english: Is it okay to take a photo here?

examples.japanese: このリンゴを食べてもいいですか。
examples.english: May I eat this apple?

examples.japanese: 試験が終わったら、帰ってもいいです。
examples.english: You can go home after the exam is over.

items.title: ～ても/でも (〜te mo/demo)
items.explanation: Expresses 'even if' or 'even though'; used to convey contradiction or contrast.
items.structure: Verb-て-form + も, い-Adjective (-い) + くても, な-Adjective + でも, Noun + でも

examples.japanese: 雨が降っても、学校に行きます。
examples.english: Even if it rains, I will go to school.

examples.japanese: この部屋が汚くても、掃除しないつもりです。
examples.english: Even if this room is dirty, I don't intend to clean it.

examples.japanese: その映画が面白くなくても、見ます。
examples.english: Even if that movie is not interesting, I will watch it.

items.title: ～といい (〜to ii)
items.explanation: Express a wish or hope; 'I hope', 'it would be good if'.
items.structure: Verb-casual + といい, い-Adjective + といい, な-Adjective + だといい, Noun + だといい

examples.japanese: 明日晴れるといいね。
examples.english: I hope it will be sunny tomorrow.

examples.japanese: この試験に合格するといい。
examples.english: I hope to pass this exam.

examples.japanese: 彼が元気だといいな。
examples.english: I hope he is doing well.

items.title: ～という (〜to iu) Noun
items.explanation: Used to define or explain a noun more specifically.
items.structure: Noun + という + Noun, な-Adjective + という + Noun, Adjectival Verb + という + Noun

examples.japanese: 彼は日本語が流暢なアメリカ人という人です。
examples.english: He is an American who speaks fluent Japanese.

examples.japanese: 昨日、美味しかったというケーキを食べました。
examples.english: Yesterday, I ate a cake that was said to be delicious.

examples.japanese: 有名な歌手という彼女は、たくさんのファンがいます。
examples.english: She, who is called a famous singer, has many fans.

items.title: どういう Noun (dou iu Noun)
items.explanation: Asking for clarification or more information about a noun; 'what kind of', 'what sort of'.

examples.japanese: どういう仕事をしていますか？
examples.english: What kind of work do you do?

examples.japanese: どういう映画が好きですか？
examples.english: What kind of movies do you like?

examples.japanese: どういう服を着たいですか？
examples.english: What kind of clothes do you want to wear?

intro.title: N4 Grammar — Group 21
intro.explanation: Learn N4 grammar points 101–105. These patterns are essential for the JLPT N4 level.

items.title: ～と思う (〜to omou)
items.explanation: Express one's thoughts or opinions; 'I think', 'I believe'.
items.structure: Verb-casual + と思う, い-Adjective + と思う, な-Adjective + だと思う, Noun + だと思う

examples.japanese: 明日晴れると思います。
examples.english: I think it will be sunny tomorrow.

examples.japanese: この映画は面白いと思う。
examples.english: I think this movie is interesting.

examples.japanese: 彼は親切だと思います。
examples.english: I think he is kind.

items.title: ～という (〜to iu)
items.explanation: Used to quote, express hearsay or define something.
items.structure: Verb-casual + という, い-Adjective + という, な-Adjective + という, Noun + という

examples.japanese: 彼は「好きだ」と言った。
examples.english: He said 'I like you'.

examples.japanese: その映画は面白いという評判があります。
examples.english: The movie has a reputation for being interesting.

examples.japanese: 日本には富士山という高い山があります。
examples.english: In Japan, there is a tall mountain called Mount Fuji.

items.title: ～ないといけない (〜nai to ikenai)
items.explanation: Express a necessity; 'must', 'have to', 'need to'.

examples.japanese: 明日試験があるから、今夜勉強しないといけない。
examples.english: I have an exam tomorrow, so I have to study tonight.

examples.japanese: ９時に出発しないといけない。
examples.english: We must leave at 9 o'clock.

examples.japanese: 風邪をひかないように、手をよく洗わないといけない。
examples.english: To avoid catching a cold, we have to wash our hands well.

items.title: ～なきゃいけない (〜nakya ikenai)
items.explanation: Express a necessity or obligation; 'must', 'have to'.
items.structure: Verb-casual (negative form without い) + なきゃいけない

examples.japanese: 明日までに宿題を終わらなきゃいけない。
examples.english: I have to finish my homework by tomorrow.

examples.japanese: もうすぐ出かけるから、急いで準備しなきゃいけない。
examples.english: We're leaving soon, so I have to hurry and get ready.

examples.japanese: このプロジェクトは来週提出しなきゃいけない。
examples.english: I must submit this project by next week.

items.title: ～なくちゃいけない (〜naku cha ikenai)
items.explanation: Express the obligation to do something; 'have to', 'must', 'need to'.
items.structure: Verb-ない form (-ない ending is dropped) + なくちゃいけない

examples.japanese: 仕事に行かなくちゃいけないので、早起きしなければなりません。
examples.english: I have to go to work, so I must wake up early.

examples.japanese: 試験があるから、勉強しなくちゃいけません。
examples.english: I have a test, so I must study.

examples.japanese: パスポートを更新しなくちゃいけないので、大使館に行かなければ。
examples.english: I have to renew my passport, so I need to go to the embassy.

intro.title: N4 Grammar — Group 22
intro.explanation: Learn N4 grammar points 106–110. These patterns are essential for the JLPT N4 level.

items.title: ～なくてはいけない (〜nakute wa ikenai)
items.explanation: Expresses the necessity or obligation; 'must', 'have to'.
items.structure: Verb-negative form + なくてはいけない

examples.japanese: 宿題をしなくてはいけない。
examples.english: I have to do my homework.

examples.japanese: この手紙を明日までに出さなくてはいけない。
examples.english: I must send this letter by tomorrow.

examples.japanese: 食べ物を無駄にしなくてはいけない。
examples.english: We must not waste food.

items.title: ～なくてもいい (〜nakutemo ii)
items.explanation: Expresses that something is not necessary to do; 'it's okay if not', 'don't have to'.

examples.japanese: コーヒーは飲まなくてもいいです。
examples.english: You don't have to drink the coffee.

examples.japanese: 宿題を今日しなくてもいいです。
examples.english: It's okay if you don't do your homework today.

examples.japanese: すぐに返事をしなくてもいいですよ。
examples.english: You don't have to reply immediately.

items.title: ～なければ ならない (〜nakereba naranai)
items.explanation: Express obligation or necessity; 'must', 'have to', 'need to'.
items.structure: Verb-ない form + なければ ならない

examples.japanese: 宿題をやらなければならない。
examples.english: I have to do my homework.

examples.japanese: 明日までにこの本を読まなければならない。
examples.english: I have to read this book by tomorrow.

examples.japanese: 授業に遅れないように、早く起きなければならない。
examples.english: I have to wake up early so I don't be late for class.

items.title: ～に (〜ni)
items.explanation: Indicates direction, destination, purpose, or time.

examples.japanese: 母は私にケーキを作りました。
examples.english: My mother made a cake for me.

examples.japanese: 彼女は東京に引っ越しました。
examples.english: She moved to Tokyo.

examples.japanese: 銀行にお金を預けます。
examples.english: I deposit money in the bank.

items.title: ～ので (〜node)
items.explanation: Express a reason or a cause for something; 'because', 'since', 'so'.
items.structure: Verb-casual + ので, い-Adjective + ので, な-Adjective + なので, Noun + なので

examples.japanese: 明日試験があるので、今晩勉強します。
examples.english: I will study tonight because there is a test tomorrow.

examples.japanese: このドレスが高いので、買わないことにします。
examples.english: I will not buy this dress because it is expensive.

examples.japanese: 田中さんは病気なので、今日は来ません。
examples.english: Tanaka-san will not come today since he is sick.

intro.title: N4 Grammar — Group 23
intro.explanation: Learn N4 grammar points 111–115. These patterns are essential for the JLPT N4 level.

items.title: ～のです (〜no desu)
items.explanation: Provides an explanation or gives background information; 'the fact is', 'the reason is', 'actually'.
items.structure: Verb-casual + のです, い-Adjective + のです, な-Adjective + なのです, Noun + なのです

examples.japanese: この本は難しいのです。
examples.english: This book is difficult, you see.

examples.japanese: 明日は忙しいのです。
examples.english: The fact is, I am busy tomorrow.

examples.japanese: 彼女は英語の先生なのです。
examples.english: The reason is, she is an English teacher.

items.title: ～のに (〜no ni)
items.explanation: Used to express contrast between expectation and reality, or to indicate a purpose for doing something
items.structure: Verb-casual + のに, い-Adjective + のに, な-Adjective + なのに, Noun + なのに

examples.japanese: 遅刻したのに、先生は怒らなかった。
examples.english: Even though I was late, the teacher didn't get angry.

examples.japanese: 彼は疲れているのに、まだ働いています。
examples.english: Despite being tired, he is still working.

examples.japanese: 勉強するのに静かな場所が必要です。
examples.english: In order to study, I need a quiet place.

items.title: ～ばいい (〜ba ii)
items.explanation: Express a suggestion or advice; 'should', 'it would be good if'.
items.structure: Verb-ば-form + いい, い-Adjective + ければいい, な-Adjective + であればいい, Noun + であればいい

examples.japanese: もっと勉強すればいい。
examples.english: You should study more.

examples.japanese: お腹が空いたら、何か食べればいい。
examples.english: If you're hungry, you should eat something.

examples.japanese: もっと速く走ればいい。
examples.english: You should run faster.

items.title: ～まで (〜made)
items.explanation: Indicates extent, 'until', 'up to', 'as far as', 'even'.
items.structure: Verb + まで, い-Adjective + まで, な-Adjective + まで, Noun + まで

examples.japanese: 仕事が終わるまで待っています。
examples.english: I will wait until work is finished.

examples.japanese: ここから駅まで歩いて10分かかります。
examples.english: It takes 10 minutes to walk from here to the station.

examples.japanese: 私は彼が成功するまで応援します。
examples.english: I will support him until he succeeds.

items.title: ～までに (〜made ni)
items.explanation: Express 'by' or 'before' a certain time or action.
items.structure: Verb-casual + までに, Noun + までに, Time expression + までに

examples.japanese: 明日の朝８時までに起きてください。
examples.english: Please wake up by 8 a.m. tomorrow.

examples.japanese: 来週の金曜日までにレポートを提出してください。
examples.english: Please submit the report by next Friday.

examples.japanese: 彼が帰るまでに料理を終わらせたい。
examples.english: I want to finish cooking before he comes back.

intro.title: N4 Grammar — Group 24
intro.explanation: Learn N4 grammar points 116–120. These patterns are essential for the JLPT N4 level.

items.title: ～まま (〜mama)
items.explanation: Express 'as it is', 'while' or 'unchanged state'.
items.structure: Verb-てform + いる+ まま, Adjective (い & な) + まま, Noun + のまま

examples.japanese: ドアを開けたまま出かけてしまった。
examples.english: I accidentally left with the door open.

examples.japanese: 彼は目覚まし時計を止めたまま寝てしまった。
examples.english: He fell asleep with the alarm clock stopped.

examples.japanese: その部屋はきれいなままにしておいてください。
examples.english: Please keep the room clean.

items.title: ～みたいだ (〜mitai da)
items.explanation: Indicates similarity, resemblance or 'like'; 'it seems', 'appears', 'looks like'.
items.structure: Verb-casual + みたいだ, い-Adjective + みたいだ, な-Adjective + みたいだ, Noun + みたいだ

examples.japanese: 彼女が病気のみたいだ。
examples.english: She seems to be sick.

examples.japanese: このドレスは高いみたいだ。
examples.english: This dress seems to be expensive.

examples.japanese: あの人は有名人みたいだ。
examples.english: That person looks like a celebrity.

items.title: ～も (〜mo)
items.explanation: Indicates 'also', 'too', or 'as well'.
items.structure: Verb-casual + も, い-Adjective + も, な-Adjective + も, Noun + も

examples.japanese: 私もお寿司が好きです。
examples.english: I also like sushi.

examples.japanese: 彼女は英語も日本語も話せます。
examples.english: She can speak both English and Japanese.

examples.japanese: その映画は面白いし、彼も見たいと言っています。
examples.english: That movie is interesting, and he also said he wants to see it.

items.title: ～ようだ (〜you da)
items.explanation: Expresses appearance, similarity or inference; 'it seems', 'it looks like', 'it appears'.
items.structure: Verb-て form + ようだ, い-Adjective (drop い) + ようだ, な-Adjective + のようだ, Noun + のようだ

examples.japanese: 彼は元気がないようだ。
examples.english: He seems to be lacking energy.

examples.japanese: この料理は美味しいようだ。
examples.english: This dish seems to be delicious.

examples.japanese: 彼女は有名人のようだ。
examples.english: She seems like a famous person.

items.title: ～んです (〜n desu)
items.explanation: Provide an explanation or reason; 'it is that', 'the thing is', 'the reason is'.
items.structure: Verb-casual + んです, い-Adjective + んです, な-Adjective + なんです, Noun + なんです

examples.japanese: 遅れたんですが、電車が遅れました。
examples.english: I was late because the train was delayed.

examples.japanese: 疲れたんです。
examples.english: I'm tired (that's why).

examples.japanese: 彼は優しいんです。
examples.english: The thing is, he is kind.

intro.title: N4 Grammar — Group 25
intro.explanation: Learn N4 grammar points 121–124. These patterns are essential for the JLPT N4 level.

items.title: 文A。そのうえ 文B。
items.explanation: Shows additional information; 'furthermore', 'besides', 'in addition'.
items.structure: Sentence A + そのうえ + Sentence B + 。

examples.japanese: このソフトウェアは使いやすい。そのうえ、価格も手ごろだ。
examples.english: This software is easy to use. Furthermore, the price is reasonable.

examples.japanese: 彼女は美人だ。そのうえ、頭もいい。
examples.english: She is beautiful. In addition, she is smart.

examples.japanese: この映画は面白い。そのうえ、俳優たちの演技も素晴らしい。
examples.english: This movie is interesting. Besides, the actors' performances are also great.

items.title: 文A。それで 文B (Bun A. Sorede Bun B)
items.explanation: Used to connect two sentences; 'So', 'That's why', 'Therefore'.

examples.japanese: 今日は暑いです。それで、エアコンをつけました。
examples.english: It is hot today. So, I turned on the air conditioner.

examples.japanese: 電車が遅れました。それで、仕事に遅れてしまいました。
examples.english: The train was delayed. That's why I was late for work.

examples.japanese: 彼は疲れている。それで、早く寝ることにした。
examples.english: He is tired. Therefore, he decided to go to bed early.

items.title: 文A。それに 文B (Bun A. Soreni Bun B)
items.explanation: Express 'in addition to; besides,' used to include additional information.
items.structure: Sentence A + それに + Sentence B

examples.japanese: 彼は頭がいい。それに、スポーツも得意だ。
examples.english: He is smart. In addition, he is good at sports.

examples.japanese: このケーキはおいしい。それに、値段も安い。
examples.english: This cake is delicious. Besides, the price is also cheap.

examples.japanese: 私は日本語が話せます。それに、韓国語も話せます。
examples.english: I can speak Japanese. On top of that, I can also speak Korean.

items.title: 文A。だから 文B (Bun A. Dakara Bun B)
items.explanation: Express reason or cause; 'because', 'so', 'therefore'.
items.structure: Sentence A + だから + Sentence B

examples.japanese: 明日は試験だ。だから今日勉強しなければならない。
examples.english: Tomorrow is the exam, so I have to study today.

examples.japanese: この料理は簡単だ。だから初心者でも作れる。
examples.english: This dish is simple, so even beginners can make it.

examples.japanese: 彼は病気だ。だから今日学校を休む。
examples.english: He is sick, so he will take a day off from school today.
